chapter.title: The Day of Judgment
chapter.summary: Christ will judge in righteousness. Study resurrection, accountability, mercy, eternal outcomes, and faithful preparation without predicting a date.
chapter.question: What does final judgment teach us about justice, mercy, and life now?

learningObjectives: Explain the principal passages in their context.
Distinguish biblical observation, theological interpretation, and artistic choices.
Apply the teaching through truthful worship and care for neighbors.

sections.title: An appointed day: read Paul’s message in Athens
paragraphs: Paul addresses people surrounded by religious images and philosophical debate. He speaks of the Creator who gives life and calls people to turn from ignorance. His announcement of a coming judgment is connected to the resurrection of the man appointed by God. The point is that history and human conduct answer to God’s righteous authority. Paul does not give a date, a seven-year chart, or a calculation from the age of the earth. The reference image rightly draws attention to Acts 17:31, but the whole speech helps us see its purpose: repentance and recognition of the living God. The resurrection is presented as assurance of the appointed judge, making this a proclamation about Jesus rather than a technique for predicting the news.

sections.title: Christ the judge and the promise of life
paragraphs: John 5 places judgment alongside the Son’s life-giving authority. Jesus speaks of hearing his word, believing the Father who sent him, and passing from death to life. He also speaks of a future summons reaching those in the tombs. Christians should read these promises and warnings together. Judgment is not simply a frightening extra attached to the Gospel; it is part of the claim that the Son will set things right. Nor should the promise of life be deleted in order to keep readers afraid. The passage grounds confidence in Christ and responsibility before him. The judge is the Son who acts in accord with the Father, not a human leader who can claim divine authority over every person’s destiny.

sections.title: Resurrection means the whole person matters
paragraphs: The hope of resurrection prevents Christian teaching about judgment from treating bodily life as disposable. John speaks about those in the tombs coming out, while Acts records a hope involving both the righteous and the unrighteous. These passages announce accountability beyond death. They do not supply a photograph of resurrection bodies or settle every question about the sequence of final events. A humane explanation should acknowledge grief and the seriousness of death without claiming private knowledge of a particular deceased person’s judgment. The practical implication is that what people do with their bodies, resources, and relationships matters. Bodily resurrection also belongs with hope: God’s purpose is not merely to abandon creation but to overcome death and establish life.

sections.title: Every person gives account: begin with ourselves
paragraphs: Romans 14 applies coming accountability to a present problem: believers despising or condemning one another over disputed practices. Paul turns attention toward each person’s own account before God and toward removing obstacles to a neighbor’s faith. Second Corinthians likewise connects appearing before Christ with a life aimed at pleasing him and compelled by his love. These contexts challenge two misuses of judgment teaching. It cannot become an excuse to claim infallible insight into another person’s heart, and it cannot make present conduct irrelevant. A concrete response is to examine dishonesty, exploitation, neglect, and cruelty in our own life, seek forgiveness, and repair harm where possible. Such action is a response to Christ’s authority and love; it is not an attempt to purchase control over the final verdict.

sections.title: Matthew 25: judgment makes mercy concrete
paragraphs: Matthew depicts the Son of Man gathering the nations and bringing hidden neglect into view. Food, welcome, clothing, and care for the sick and imprisoned become concrete matters of response to the king. The text cannot honestly be reduced to passing a religious vocabulary test. Christians debate the precise identity of the least brothers and how this scene relates to other judgment passages, so that question belongs in careful study. Still, the scene gives no permission for indifference to suffering. Read it alongside Ephesians 2:8–10: salvation is God’s gift, and those made new in Christ are created for good works. Grace and accountable action belong together without turning acts of compassion into a price list for eternal life.

sections.title: The throne, the books, and the book of life
paragraphs: Revelation’s great white throne scene places the great and small before the same authority. The opened books present deeds as knowable before God, while the book of life gives the scene a further distinction that should not be collapsed into a simple scorekeeping chart. Death and Hades themselves face their end. This visionary language announces the defeat of powers that enslave creation and the seriousness of evil. It is not a technical description of heavenly furniture or a mechanism by which a minister can read a person’s unseen record. The illustration deliberately leaves the throne unoccupied: it evokes the passage’s setting without pretending to provide a likeness of God. Read the vision’s own words before deciding how its details fit a particular end-times system.

sections.title: Eternal outcomes: speak with seriousness and care
paragraphs: Matthew contrasts eternal punishment with eternal life. Revelation places its warnings beside a new creation where death and mourning end. John joins Jesus’ saving mission with the seriousness of rejecting his words. These texts should neither be trivialized nor used to terrify people into submission to a human leader. Christian traditions debate the nature and duration of punishment and the relation between final judgment and intermediate states. A textbook should name those debates without pretending that one screenshot settles them. This lesson affirms the gravity of judgment and the hope of life with God within its stated Christian framework. It does not pronounce the final destiny of particular individuals, and it does not make a graphic portrayal of torment into a substitute for understanding the passages.

sections.title: Prepare through faithfulness, not date-setting
paragraphs: Readiness is expressed through repentance, trust, patient hope, and a life turned toward God and neighbor. Matthew’s warning about the unknown day and hour resists precise prediction. Second Peter uses the comparison between a day and a thousand years in a discussion of God’s patience; it does not instruct readers to convert the creation week into a calendar for the return of Christ. Hebrews places judgment alongside Christ’s once-for-all offering and the expectation of his appearing for salvation. These connections keep hope close to the warning. A practical study response is to reconcile with someone, address a neglected responsibility, and ask for pastoral help where needed. Preparation should produce truthful and compassionate living, not panic, speculative dates, or abandonment of ordinary obligations.

glossaryEntries.note: Specific sequences and outcomes require confessional review.

quiz.question: What does Acts 17:31 announce?
options: An appointed righteous judgment associated with the risen Jesus
An exact date for the end
A command to stop caring for neighbors
quiz.explanation: Paul connects judgment with repentance and resurrection.

quiz.question: What does Romans 14 ask us to remember?
options: Each person gives account to God
quiz.explanation: Accountability is a reason for humility and care.

quiz.question: What is prominent in Matthew 25?
options: Concrete acts of mercy and neglect
quiz.explanation: Food, welcome, clothing, and visiting are concrete concerns.

quiz.question: Why is the illustrated throne empty?
options: The artwork does not claim a likeness of God
The passage says there is no judge
quiz.explanation: An illustration can evoke the setting without representing God.

quiz.question: How should Christians prepare?
options: Repentance, faithfulness, and love without date-setting
quiz.explanation: Read Matthew 24:36 alongside the call to faithful living.

fil.title: Ang Araw ng Paghuhukom
fil.summary: Pag-aralan ang matuwid na paghuhukom ni Cristo, muling pagkabuhay, pananagutan, awa, at paghahanda nang walang paghula ng petsa.
fil.question: Ano ang itinuturo ng mga talata at paano ito isasabuhay?

appointed-day.title: Ang itinakdang araw
paragraphs: Sa Mga Gawa 17:22–31, ipinakikilala ni Pablo ang Maylikha at nananawagan ng pagsisisi. Iniuugnay niya ang darating na matuwid na paghuhukom sa muling pagkabuhay ng hinirang ng Diyos. Hindi siya nagbibigay ng petsa o pormulang panghula.

christ-the-judge.title: Si Cristo na hukom at tagapagbigay-buhay
paragraphs: Magkasamang tinatalakay ng Juan 5:22–30 ang kapangyarihan ng Anak na humatol at magbigay-buhay. May pangako sa nakikinig at sumasampalataya, at may darating na pagtawag sa mga nasa libingan. Basahin nang magkasama ang pangako at babala.

resurrection.title: Ang muling pagkabuhay
paragraphs: Binabanggit ng Juan 5:28–29 at Mga Gawa 24:15 ang muling pagkabuhay at pananagutan lampas sa kamatayan. Mahalaga ang buong tao at ang ginagawa natin sa katawan at pakikipagkapwa. Hindi nagbibigay ang mga talata ng larawan ng katawan sa muling pagkabuhay o hatol sa isang tiyak na namatay.

accountability.title: Pananagutan: magsimula sa sarili
paragraphs: Sa Roma 14:10–13, ginagamit ni Pablo ang pananagutan sa Diyos upang pigilan ang paghamak sa kapatid. Sa 2 Corinto 5, iniuugnay ito sa pamumuhay na kalugud-lugod kay Cristo at inuudyukan ng kanyang pag-ibig. Suriin ang sariling gawain, humingi ng tawad, at ituwid ang pinsalang nagawa.

mercy-and-works.title: Ginagawang kongkreto ng Mateo 25 ang awa
paragraphs: Binabanggit ng Mateo 25:31–46 ang pagkain, pagtanggap sa dayuhan, pananamit, at pagdalaw sa nangangailangan. Hindi maliit na bagay ang pagpapabaya. Kasabay nito, itinuturo ng Efeso 2:8–10 na kaloob ang kaligtasan at nilikha tayo kay Cristo para sa mabubuting gawa. Hindi binibili ng awa ang buhay na walang hanggan.

books-and-life.title: Ang trono at mga aklat
paragraphs: Sa Apocalipsis 20:11–15, kapwa humaharap ang dakila at maliit sa iisang kapangyarihan. Binubuksan ang mga aklat at ang aklat ng buhay; pati kamatayan at Hades ay haharap sa wakas. Pangitain ito, hindi teknikal na plano ng langit. Sadyang walang nakaupo sa larawan upang hindi ito magkunwaring larawan ng Diyos.

outcomes-and-differences.title: Mga kahihinatnan at pag-iingat
paragraphs: Pinaghahambing ng Mateo 25:46 ang kaparusahan at buhay na walang hanggan. Inilalapit naman ng Apocalipsis 21 ang pag-asa ng bagong paglikha. May mga pagtatalo sa mga tradisyong Kristiyano tungkol sa likas at tagal ng kaparusahan. Dapat ituro ang mga talata nang seryoso at maingat, nang walang pang-aabuso sa takot o paghatol sa tiyak na tao.

prepare-without-dates.title: Maghanda nang tapat, hindi sa paghula ng petsa
paragraphs: Ang paghahanda ay pagsisisi, pagtitiwala, pag-asa, at tapat na pag-ibig sa kapwa. Hindi alam ang araw at oras sa Mateo 24:36. Ang paghahambing ng araw at sanlibong taon sa 2 Pedro 3 ay tungkol sa pagtitiis ng Diyos, hindi pormula sa pagkalkula ng pagbabalik ni Cristo.

ilo.title: Ti Aldaw ti Panangukom
ilo.summary: Adalen ti nalinteg a panangukom ni Cristo, panagungar, panagsungbat, asi, ken panagsagana nga awan panangikeddeng petsa.
ilo.question: Ania ti isuro dagiti teksto ken kasano a pagbiagan daytoy?

appointed-day.title: Ti naituding nga aldaw
paragraphs: Iti Aramid 17:22–31, iyammo ni Pablo ti Namarsua ken awisenna dagiti tattao nga agbabawi. Ikonektana ti umay a nalinteg a panangukom iti panagungar ti pinili ti Dios. Saan nga itedna ti petsa wenno pormula ti panagipadto.

christ-the-judge.title: Ni Cristo a mangukom ken mangted biag
paragraphs: Ti Juan 5:22–30 pagnaigenna ti turay ti Anak nga agukom ken mangted biag. Adda kari para iti dumngeg ken mamati, ken adda umay a panangayab kadagiti adda iti tanem. Basaen a sangsangkamaysa ti kari ken ballaag.

resurrection.title: Ti panagungar
paragraphs: Ti Juan 5:28–29 ken Aramid 24:15 ibagada ti panagungar ken panagsungbat iti labes ti patay. Napateg ti sibubukel a tao ken ti aramidtayo iti bagi ken pannakilangen. Saan nga ited dagitoy ti ladawan ti bagi iti panagungar wenno ukom iti maysa a natay.

accountability.title: Panagsungbat: rugian iti bagitayo
paragraphs: Iti Roma 14:10–13, usaren ni Pablo ti panagsungbat iti Dios tapno maliklikan ti panangumsi iti kabsat. Iti 2 Corinto 5, mainaig daytoy iti biag a makaay-ayo ken Cristo ken iturturong ti ayatna. Sukimaten ti aramid, agkiddaw pammakawan, ken ilinteg ti nadangran no mabalin.

mercy-and-works.title: Ti Mateo 25 ken ti asi
paragraphs: Iti Mateo 25:31–46, napateg ti taraon, panangawat iti ganggannaet, bado, ken panangbisita iti agkasapulan. Saan a bassit a banag ti panangbaybay-a. Ti Efeso 2:8–10 isurona a sagut ti pannakaisalakan ken naparsuatayo ken Cristo para iti naimbag nga aramid. Saan a magatang ti biag nga agnanayon babaen iti asi.

books-and-life.title: Ti trono ken dagiti libro
paragraphs: Iti Apocalipsis 20:11–15, agpadang agparang dagiti dakkel ken babassit iti maymaysa a turay. Maluktan dagiti libro ken ti libro ti biag; uray patay ken Hades ket agpatingga. Sirmata daytoy, saan a teknikal a plano ti langit. Awan ti nakatugaw iti ladawan tapno saan nga iparang a ladawan ti Dios.

outcomes-and-differences.title: Dagiti pagbanagan ken panagannad
paragraphs: Ti Mateo 25:46 pagdiligenna ti dusa ken biag nga agnanayon. Ti Apocalipsis 21 ipakitana ti namnama ti baro a panagparsua. Adda panagdidinnuma kadagiti tradision a Kristiano maipapan iti kasasaad ken kapaut ti dusa. Masapul ti naserioso ken naannad a panangisuro nga awan panangabuso iti buteng wenno panangukom iti partikular a tao.

prepare-without-dates.title: Agsagana a napudno, saan a mangikeddeng petsa
paragraphs: Ti panagsagana ket panagbabawi, panagtalek, namnama, ken napudno nga ayat iti pada a tao. Awan makaammo iti aldaw ken oras iti Mateo 24:36. Ti panangidilig iti aldaw ken sangaribu a tawen iti 2 Pedro 3 ket maipapan iti anus ti Dios, saan a pormula ti petsa ti panagsubli ni Cristo.
